faults.name: Plant foot far behind the ball
faults.threshold_source: heuristic: the extracted norms give the plant foot's position in cm (e.g. N-027, N-031), and converting needs a leg length in cm that a video doesn't give. A quarter of a leg length behind the ball centre is an uncalibrated guess, and this feature's accuracy has not been measured against labels (E2 doesn't score it).

q07.answer: To stop leaning back when you shoot, try to keep your head and the knee of your kicking foot directly over the ball, and make sure not to lean your upper body backward [K-12]. It also helps to plant your non-kicking foot right next to the ball so your body stays balanced over it rather than falling away [K-09].

args.query: drill to stop leaning back trunk lean

passages.text: To keep the ball on the ground: 1. Keep your head and the knee of your kicking foot over the ball. 2. Do not lean back.
passages.source: Special Olympics, Football Coaching Guide (2021), p. 75, Passing, Notes

passages.text: Player cannot get power or accuracy when shooting. 1. Make sure player plants non-kicking foot next to the ball. 2. Make sure knee on kicking leg is over the ball. Kick through the ball.
passages.source: Special Olympics North Carolina, Soccer Shooting Basics (2025), p. 2, Shooting Faults & Fixes, row 2 (error and correction)

passages.text: The formation of the dynamic tension arc involved: 1) kick-side hip over-extension and knee flexion, 2) trunk twist towards non-kick-side, and 3) non-kick-side shoulder extension and abduction (Figure 4, left). The release of the arc consisted of: 1) quasi whip-like control sequence of the kicking leg, and 2) upper trunk flexion and twist towards kick-side, and 3) the non-kick-side shoulder flexion and adduction during kick (Figure 4, right).
passages.source: Shan & Zhang (2011), BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil 3:23, a review, 3D Analysis, para. 2

q08.answer: Try this drill to help you get your standing foot in the right place: stand with your non-kicking foot right next to the ball, and then do a phantom kick with your kicking foot [K-10].

args.query: plant foot place position drill exercise

passages.text: 1. Have player stand with non-kicking foot next to the ball. 2. Phantom kick the ball with kicking foot.
passages.source: Special Olympics North Carolina, Soccer Shooting Basics (2025), p. 2, Shooting Faults & Fixes, row 2 (drill)

passages.text: When using their preferred leg to perform an instep kick, soccer players practise a straighter approach to the ball, place their standing foot closer to the ball, and kick the ball with greater pelvic tilt and greater knee extension of the kicking leg. Variations in the placement of the support leg impact the speed of the ball.
passages.source: Kapidžić, Huremović & Biberovic (2014), J Hum Kinet 42:81-90, Introduction, para. 3

passages.text: Another important aspect of kicking success is the placement of the support foot behind and beside the ball. There is no general consensus regarding the placement of ball beside the foot. It has been suggested that the foot should land 5-10 cm behind and 5 – 28 cm beside the ball (Hay, 1993). However, this information has not been confirmed experimentally.
passages.source: Kellis & Katis (2007), J Sports Sci Med 6(2):154-165, a review, p. 162
